result.markdown:
If you have slipped and fallen in a shopping centre in Hobart, you may be entitled to public liability compensation if the shopping centre management or occupier failed to maintain a safe environment (e.g., failing to clean up a spill or fix a hazard in a timely manner).[hallpayne.com.au](https://hallpayne.com.au/areas-of-practice/personal-injury/tas/public-liability/#:~:text=School%20yard%20accidents.%20Dog%20attacks.%20Slips%20and,shopping%20centre%29%20Boating%20%28marine%29%20accidents.%20Road%20accidents.)

Several reputable law firms in Hobart handle public liability and slip-and-fall claims, many of which operate on a **"No Win, No Fee"** basis.[lawconnect.com](https://lawconnect.com/en-au/find/public-liability-and-claims/tas/hobart-7000#:~:text=The%20firm%20is%20recognised%20for%20its%20success,No%20Fee%20policy%20and%20free%20claim%20evaluations.)

They specialize explicitly in slip-and-fall incidents in shopping centres and supermarkets.[www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/public-liability/public-liability-lawyers-in-hobart#:~:text=You'll%20have%20the%20support%20of%20locals%20with,You%20were%20injured%20by%20a%20dog%2Fanimal%20attack.)
  * *Key Feature:* Operates on a No Win, No Fee basis and offers free initial claim checks.[www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/public-liability/public-liability-lawyers-in-hobart#:~:text=Simply%20answer%20a%20few%20questions%20online%20to,enquiry%20Call%20us%20on%201800%20444%20141.)

---

### Crucial Steps to Take Right Now

1.  **Prioritize Your Health:** Ensure you have seen a doctor or visited a hospital to document your injuries properly. Medical records are critical evidence for your claim.
2.  **Report the Incident:** If you haven't already, report the fall to the shopping centre management or centre security and request a copy of the incident report.
3.  **Gather Evidence:** Take photos of the hazard (if possible or if it still exists), keep the shoes and clothing you were wearing, and collect contact details of any witnesses.
4.  **Mind the Time Limits:** In Tasmania, strict statutory time limits apply to personal injury and public liability claims. It is best to consult a lawyer promptly.
